_readme: SAIRNlaw deadline engine seed -- Ohio civil litigation (Ohio Rules of Civil
Procedure). Phase 3, state jurisdiction #1 of 4 (OH/IN/MI/PA), Ohio only in
this file -- seeded and verified one state at a time per standing
instruction, not batched.
Loaded the same way as the federal seed: through api/legal-deadlines.js's
add_rule / add_holidays actions, which reject any rule lacking an authority
URL and stamp verified_by from the real session.
Every value below was read from a primary or near-primary source on
2026-08-21 and is quoted in the row. None came from memory or assumed to
carry over from the federal seed.
REAL DIVERGENCE FROM FRCP, VERIFIED BEFORE ENCODING (not assumed the same
just because the rule text reads similarly):
1. OHIO NEVER ADOPTED THE 2009 FEDERAL AMENDMENT. Civ.R. 6(A): 'When the
period of time prescribed or allowed is less than seven days,
intermediate Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays shall be excluded in
the computation.' FRCP 6(a) dropped this mechanism entirely in 2009 (see
sairnlaw_deadline_seed_us_federal.json and deadline-engine.js's own
header) -- Ohio's version is a live, in-force state rule, not a stale
leftover of the same kind. Encoded as a NEW computation standard,
ohio_civ_r_6a, not mapped onto frcp_6a -- mapping it would have silently
dropped the exclusion and produced dates LATER than the true deadline
on every Ohio period under 7 days, the dangerous direction.
2. OHIO'S STANDARD ANSWER DEADLINE IS 28 DAYS, NOT 30 OR 21. Civ.R.
12(A)(1): 'The defendant shall serve his answer within twenty-eight days
after service of the summons and complaint upon him.' Verified directly
rather than assumed to mirror FRCP 12(a)(1)(A)(i)'s 21 days.
3. OHIO'S MAIL-SERVICE EXTENSION (Civ.R. 6(D)) DOES NOT APPLY TO THE ANSWER
RULE SEEDED HERE. Civ.R. 6(D) adds three days for service 'by mail or
commercial carrier service under Civ.R. 5(B)(2)(c) or (d)', but its own
text carves out an exception: it 'does not apply to responses to service
of summons under Rules 4 through 4.6.' The rule seeded here (Civ.R.
12(A)(1)) is triggered BY service of summons, so it is exactly the
excluded case. No service_extension is attached to this rule --
deliberate, same discipline as Phase 1's FRCP waiver/6(d) omission, not
an oversight. Civ.R. 6(D) itself is not yet encoded as a
SERVICE_EXTENSION_STANDARD in the engine because no seeded Ohio rule
yet qualifies for it -- building it now would be speculative capability
with nothing to exercise it.
4. OHIO'S HOLIDAY CALENDAR IS NOT THE FEDERAL ONE, verified date-by-date
rather than copied. O.R.C. 1.14 lists the same 11 named holidays as the
federal calendar (Washington-Lincoln Day is Ohio's name for the same
third-Monday-in-February date as the federal Washington's Birthday) but
the SHIFT RULE differs: O.R.C. 1.14 states 'If any day designated in
this section as a legal holiday falls on Sunday, the next succeeding day
is a legal holiday' -- a Sunday-only shift. Unlike 5 U.S.C. 6103 (the
federal statute), O.R.C. 1.14 has NO Saturday-to-Friday shift provision.
Checked day-of-week for every fixed-date holiday in 2026-2027 (not
assumed): Independence Day 2026 (Sat) and Juneteenth + Christmas 2027
(both Sat) stay on their actual dates under Ohio law rather than moving
to the preceding Friday the way the federal calendar already loaded in
this system observes them. Independence Day 2027 (Sun) shifts to Monday
under BOTH rules, so that one date matches federal by coincidence, not
because the rule is the same. Holiday `kind` is 'declared' rather than
'state' for every entry here -- the 'state' kind's direction-dependent
exclusion (holidayFor's FRCP 6(a)(6) accommodation for a federal court
sitting within a state) is a federal-specific concept with no Ohio
analog; Ohio's own courts observe Ohio's own holidays regardless of
counting direction, so a kind that always counts is the correct choice,
not a mislabeling of these as federally-declared days.
STILL OPEN, NOT IN THIS FILE: Indiana Trial Rule 6, Michigan MCR 1.108, and
Pennsylvania (rule-number conflict between Pa.R.C.P. 106 and 201 Pa. Code
Section 107 not yet resolved) -- each needs its own verification pass
before being seeded, per the same discipline applied to Ohio here.

rules.label: Answer to a complaint after service of summons and complaint (Ohio)

authority.quote: The defendant shall serve his answer within twenty-eight days after service of the summons and complaint upon him.
authority.note: No service_extension attached -- Civ.R. 6(D)'s own text excludes responses to service of summons under Rules 4 through 4.6, and this rule's trigger IS service of summons. See _readme item 3. DISCLOSED LIMITATION on effective_from: the CURRENT 28-day text was confirmed live on 2026-08-21 and Ohio's civil rules as a body took effect 1970-07-01 (confirmed), but the specific day-count's own unbroken amendment history between 1970 and today was NOT independently traced -- one source indicates Rule 12 was amended 1983-07-01 without confirming which subsection or whether the day-count changed. effective_from is set to the rule-set's original adoption date as the best-sourced anchor available rather than a guessed later date; this is safe for any matter triggered in the modern era (the live-proof compute below uses 2026) but a matter triggered before Rule 12's actual last substantive amendment to this subsection should have that amendment date confirmed independently before relying on this row.

Sunday-only shift (no Saturday shift, unlike the federal 5 U.S.C. 6103 calendar already loaded under 'us-federal'). Every date checked by day-of-week for 2026, not copied from the federal list. Independence Day 2026 falls on a Saturday and is NOT shifted under Ohio law, unlike the federal calendar's 2026-07-03 (observed) entry.

Loaded alongside 2026 for the same cross-year reason as the federal calendar. Juneteenth 2027 and Christmas 2027 both fall on a Saturday and are NOT shifted under Ohio law (unlike federal's 2027-06-18 and 2027-12-24 observed entries). Independence Day 2027 falls on a Sunday and DOES shift to Monday under Ohio's own Sunday-shift provision, matching the federal date in this one instance only.
